key_insight: In β-Sn, twin-boundary faceting on (301) twins is driven by absorption of <c> dislocations, with facet length increasing as more dislocations are absorbed.
engineering_relevance: This mechanism helps explain and potentially control deformation and strengthening in Sn-based solder alloys, especially under dislocation-rich loading conditions.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of β-Sn twin-boundary behavior
Use of a machine-learned interatomic potential trained for the material
Comparison against isotropic elasticity theory including disclination effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation results showing a dislocation-absorption-mediated faceting reaction and that the predicted facet length matches elasticity theory only when disclination character is included.
watch_item: The mechanism is inferred from simulation and theory for a specific boundary orientation, so broader applicability to other loading paths or microstructures should be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Dislocation mediated twin boundary faceting in $β$-Sn
